title: Data Engineer

Comfortable communicating with senior leaders.

Comfortable presenting technical changes to CAB.

We're becoming an AI-native company, a commitment that means you'll be empowered (and expected) to use AI tools and thinking in your day-to-day work. You'll have the training, support, and freedom to use AI responsibly and creatively to spark ideas, solve problems faster, and unlock new ways of working.
 
If you’re passionate about creating solutions that put people first and helping businesses and their teams thrive, join us at Deputy and make an impact where it matters most!
Responsibilities
Tool Orchestration: You are the Platform Owner for our Data Catalogue and Governance layer, ensuring seamless integration across the modern data stack and intelligent automation.
Taxonomy & Knowledge Graph: Design and maintain a universal Business Glossary and Technical Metadata schema. You will ensure that every asset has defined ownership, lineage, and semantic meaning. You will strategise how to scale and automate the underlying processes using AI (eg. AI-generated attribute definitions)
Data Discovery: Improve the "Time-to-Insight" by optimizing searchability and documentation, ensuring that downstream users can autonomously find and verify the data they need. You will leverage Agentic AI to enhance this autonomy with calculated risk of accuracy and consistency.
Quality-as-Code: Partner with Analytics Engineers to embed dbt tests and automated quality assertions into our CI/CD pipelines, aligning with the DAMA Data Quality dimensions (Accuracy, Completeness, Consistency, etc.).
Lineage & Impact Analysis: Utilize our data catalogue to monitor end-to-end data lineage, performing proactive impact analysis to ensure upstream changes don't break downstream "Sources of Truth."
Reference Data Management: Standardize reference data sets across our tech stack to ensure "one version of the truth" for dimensions like Currency, Geography, and Billing Structure.
Data Classification: Operationalise PII/Sensitive data identification. You will implement automated tagging and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) / Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to mitigate risk without slowing down analysis.
Stewardship & Accountability: Facilitate Data Stewardship by partnering with department heads to enable Data Owners, establishing clear RACI models for data domains.
Lifecycle Execution: Platform enablement of data lifecycle management across landing, transformation, and access data layers.
Skills & Experience
Experience: 2–5 years in Data Governance, Analytics Engineering, or Data Management. Familiarity with DAMA DMBOK frameworks is highly preferred.
Technical Mastery: Advanced SQL and hands-on experience with dbt (Data Build Tool). You must be able to read and audit transformation logic.
Applied AI: Proven experience of architecting and implementing intelligent automation and agentic AI patterns in processes and tooling
Governance Architecture: Proven experience implementing enterprise-grade catalogs such as Databricks Unity Catalog or similar (Alation, Collibra, DataHub).
Risk & Privacy Fluency: A technical understanding of how to map GDPR, SOC2, and ISO 27001 requirements to physical data structures and access patterns.
SaaS Ecosystems: Experience managing data flowing through high-volume integration tools like Fivetran, Stitch, or Airbyte.
Data Infrastructure: Databricks (Unity Catalog), AWS S3, Redshift.
Data Modeling: dbt (Core or Cloud), SQL.

Deputy is a global SaaS workforce management company with hubs in Sydney, Melbourne, San Francisco and London, plus team members working remotely across the United States. Our platform serves over 1.5 million workers and 375,000 workplaces across 100+ countries. We are backed by top global investors and recently achieved Unicorn status. 
At Deputy, we’re improving the world of work, one shift at a time, for 80% of the world’s workforce: hourly workers. These are the dedicated employees who keep our world running – from baristas to nurses, cleaners to delivery drivers, florists to factory workers. Despite their vital role in society, most workplace technology has focused on those workers who sit behind a desk, but at Deputy, we transform the frontline. When businesses use Deputy, their workplaces thrive – the business is more profitable, compliant, and productive, while the workers are more engaged and happier at work.
We're becoming an AI-native company, a commitment that means you'll be empowered (and expected) to use AI tools and thinking in your day-to-day work. You'll have the training, support, and freedom to use AI responsibly and creatively to spark ideas, solve problems faster, and unlock new ways of working.
If you’re passionate about creating solutions that put people first and helping businesses and their teams thrive, join us at Deputy and make an impact where it matters most!
As our Data Management Analyst, you will be the primary architect of Deputy’s Data Governance Framework, operating at the intersection of Data Engineering and Business Intelligence with the empowerment of AI. Aligned with DAMA DMBOK standards, you will lead the deployment of our metadata and governance platforms, infrastructure and processes. Your mission is to transform our data estate into a formal "Data Asset," ensuring structural integrity, high discoverability, and rigorous quality standards to fuel Deputy’s global scaling.
This role sits within the Data Team with a company-wide mandate to architect Data Governance with a special focus on Metadata Management, Data Quality and Data Risk. You will lead the implementation of our "Governance-as-Code" approach using an organisation-wide Data Governance platform (eg. Unity Catalog/Data Hub) and embedding AI-native processes/tooling. While you are not the perimeter security officer, you are the Data Custodian responsible for the identification, classification, and lifecycle management of sensitive information (PII/PHI). You will bridge the gap between raw data ingestion and curated, governed Data Products that the entire organization can trust.
You are a technical analyst who views the DAMA DMBOK Knowledge Areas—particularly Metadata, Quality, and Risk - as foundational engineering requirements. You believe in "Governance by Design," building automated guardrails within the transformation layer rather than manual gates at the finish line. You leverage Artificial Intelligence across people, process and technology where there is clear business value and strategic impact. You are motivated by turning "Dark Data" into searchable, high-utility assets and thrive in complex environments where you can bridge technical debt with scalable structural solutions.
Responsibilities
Metadata Management & Discovery
Tool Orchestration: You are the Platform Owner for our Data Catalogue and Governance layer, ensuring seamless integration across the modern data stack and intelligent automation.
Taxonomy & Knowledge Graph: Design and maintain a universal Business Glossary and Technical Metadata schema. You will ensure that every asset has defined ownership, lineage, and semantic meaning. You will strategise how to scale and automate the underlying processes using AI (eg. AI-generated attribute definitions)
Data Discovery: Improve the "Time-to-Insight" by optimizing searchability and documentation, ensuring that downstream users can autonomously find and verify the data they need. You will leverage Agentic AI to enhance this autonomy with calculated risk of accuracy and consistency.
Data Quality & Analytics Engineering
Quality-as-Code: Partner with Analytics Engineers to embed dbt tests and automated quality assertions into our CI/CD pipelines, aligning with the DAMA Data Quality dimensions (Accuracy, Completeness, Consistency, etc.).
Lineage & Impact Analysis: Utilize our data catalogue to monitor end-to-end data lineage, performing proactive impact analysis to ensure upstream changes don't break downstream "Sources of Truth."
Reference Data Management: Standardize reference data sets across our tech stack to ensure "one version of the truth" for dimensions like Currency, Geography, and Billing Structure.
Data Risk, Privacy & Lifecycle Implementation
Data Classification: Operationalise PII/Sensitive data identification. You will implement automated tagging and Attribute-Based Access Control (ABAC) / Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) to mitigate risk without slowing down analysis.
Stewardship & Accountability: Facilitate Data Stewardship by partnering with department heads to enable Data Owners, establishing clear RACI models for data domains.
Lifecycle Execution: Platform enablement of data lifecycle management across landing, transformation, and access data layers.
Skills & Experience
Experience: 2–5 years in Data Governance, Analytics Engineering, or Data Management. Familiarity with DAMA DMBOK frameworks is highly preferred.
Technical Mastery: Advanced SQL and hands-on experience with dbt (Data Build Tool). You must be able to read and audit transformation logic.
Applied AI: Proven experience of architecting and implementing intelligent automation and agentic AI patterns in processes and tooling
Governance Architecture: Proven experience implementing enterprise-grade catalogs such as Databricks Unity Catalog or similar (Alation, Collibra, DataHub).
Risk & Privacy Fluency: A technical understanding of how to map GDPR, SOC2, and ISO 27001 requirements to physical data structures and access patterns.
SaaS Ecosystems: Experience managing data flowing through high-volume integration tools like Fivetran, Stitch, or Airbyte.

Data Infrastructure: Databricks (Unity Catalog), AWS S3, Redshift.

This is a rare role. It sits at the intersection of financial accounting and the data-driven future for a well established vertically integrated luxury business spanning raw material sourcing, artisan manufacturing, and multi-boutique retail.
If you have the accounting fundamentals and you're curious about, studying, or already working in - automated analytics, AI, or data intelligence, this was written for you.
Finance background is non-negotiable.
Before anything else - if you do not have hands-on finance experience owning BAS preparation, month-end journals, and compliance end-to-end, this role is not for you. The accounting foundation is not a stepping stone. It is the job.
The business operates across multiple entities and three states. The finance function is being deliberately reimagined - systems will be structured, and the cost intelligence layer for the product range is a focus. This role sits at the centre.
In this role you own the technical accounting engine - compliance, month-end, costings, COGS, and reporting. The mandate sitting underneath all of that is to consider 'can this be automated?' before accepting old manual processes - and to help build the answer.
The diverse product cycle journey includes traditional artisan elements that require precision and craft, while there is a significant data-driven layer as the foundational element deliberately and urgently alongside them. Most finance people never get close to a product like this.
The Role
As Finance & Data Analyst you are responsible for the technical accounting engine of the business - compliance, month-end, costings, COGS, and reporting - across a multi-entity group structure.
The finance function is a focus. Xero is being optimised. Payroll & HR systems are being re-imagined. The cost model for the product range does not yet exist as a finance-owned document. You will help build it.
As systems bed in, the role evolves. The compliance work stays yours - but the time you spend on it shrinks as automation takes over the repeatable work. You shift from doing reconciliations to building the systems that do them. Month one to month eight: that is a tracked plan, not a vague aspiration.
What We're Looking For
The non-negotiables:
3+ years owning a finance function end-to-end
BAS preparation experience
Advanced Xero - multi-entity experience strongly preferred
Month-end journals drafted independently
Australian GST and payroll compliance - solid and current
The data and automation spectrum:
We are not looking for one specific profile. From genuinely curious and just getting started, to building with Power BI, n8n, or Spotlight, to technically proficient in Python or SQL alongside your accounting - all are welcome. Tell us honestly where you sit and where you want to go.
What will make you stand out: you can point to something specific you have automated or built in a finance context, however small. A report. A reconciliation. A workflow. Something real.
Manufacturing or product business background is a strong advantage - you understand how cost flows through a physical product.
How You Work - This Matters as Much as What You Know
This role operates inside a function being rebuilt in real time. We need someone who moves with the business, not ahead or behind it.
You communicate upward clearly and proactively.
When implementing something new, you align first, then act.
You manage your own workload with structure - deadlines are visible, progress is reported, problems are surfaced early.
You present problems with a recommended solution attached.
If you work autonomously but collaboratively - moving with pace while keeping the right people informed - this will feel natural. If you prefer to work independently and present outcomes at the end, this is probably not the right fit.
Why This Role
Own the numbers behind a product that goes from raw material to boutique window
A genuine mandate to bring data intelligence and automation into the finance function
Real variety: compliance, costings, COGS, automation builds, inventory intelligence
Salary flexible for the right combination of skills, we are seeking talent

title: Data Analyst Intern Data Insights and Analytics
description:
Data Analyst Intern (Data Insights and Analytics)
We are inviting selected students (BA, MS) in Data Science to be part of pioneering the cloud, data, AI and web3 space. You will have the opportunity to contribute to the development of one of the world's first large-scale open data clouds and analytics engines. Openmesh is a dedicated global initiative that brings together brilliant minds in the tech industry to create open data and open infrastructures that will be pivotal in shaping the next10-20years.
This internship can be used for your 400 hours of industry experience (PEP 40). This is a 2-12 weeks paid internship to begin soon. The role will take place in our Sydney George St. Office. Unlock your career potential by working with a world class team, opportunity for permanent job placements, competitive salaries, and exciting cash prize competitions!
About Openmesh and Xnode
Today a handful of corporations control 90% of the world's data and IT infrastructure and we are expected to trust them. This is not just bad for business; it's bad for everyone. Information asymmetry has led to social inequality, scandals, polarization, and corruption. Sometimes, it has even led to war. Centralized data control acts as a potential chokepoint for innovation, raises privacy concerns, and creates a bottleneck for the free flow of data.
Openmesh is a cutting-edge new open-source cloud infrastructure and a global open data network aimed at storing important global data without a middleman. It is the largest open web3 data lake, covering approximately 80% of the entire crypto and web3 ecosystem today. In 2023 and 2024, we aim to expand our data coverage to include public health and scientific research data.
Openmesh enables anyone to create their own decentralized data cloud, connect globally, share data securely, slash deployment costs, and automate data cloud setup. The Openmesh Network is designed to collect, store, process, stream, and provide data connectivity for anyone, anywhere, anytime, without the need for registration, licensing, or payments. Think of Openmesh as the internet's open data fabric. It grants universal access and prevents interferences created by regulators, governments, corporations, and even its own creators. The possibilities are endless.
Core Products
Our flagship product, Xnode, is an integral part of this vision, offering a revolutionary platform for developers to build decentralized data clouds. Xnode, enables developers to build their own decentralized data clouds with data connectivity, data APIs, and query & analytics engines in mere minutes, instead of weeks or months. They pay only for computing and storage, sidestepping licensing and setup fees. Xnode facilitates a 10-15 fold cost reduction in running and operating data clouds and can save over 95% of deployment time.
Pythia is a powerhouse analytics & query engine that transforms raw data into actionable insights. Pythia allows anyone to design, build, visualize, and deploy powerful data products.
Unified APIs provide a single endpoint for all crypto & web3 data, making it accessible to anyone, anywhere, without any costs. There are no licenses, registrations, or setup fees involved.
Our vision
Our vision is to democratize data and address information asymmetry at a scale. Data & information is the most valuable commodity in the world. Without quality, reliable data, all webpages, apps, and the entire internet will stop working. We believe access to reliable, unedited information is a fundamental right- an aspect of a free and democratic society. The Core Principles of Openmesh, by design, has no single authority that can alter its data, how the information is distributed or controlled, or who can see what and when. The infrastructure and entire technology stack is open-source and governed by an open-source community.
The opportunity
Leverage this paid internship opportunity to fulfill your PEP 40H industry experience requirement.
Learn groundbreaking innovations in Data, Cloud, Blockchain, AI, and Web3 Infrastructure from visionaries, senior engineers, product owners and discover what your dream job is really like.
You will be given access to our open source technology, hackathons, virtual conferences, mentoring sessions, R&D infrastructure, workshops, and an opportunity to observe and apply your knowledge in practice. You have the option to work in person or remotely. There is an upcoming hackathon on the 28th.
Career Progression - top-performing candidates will receive a full-time offer.
Gain on-the-job experience. You'll be assigned a project that will develop your problem-solving skills, teach you how to present your ideas, work with a team, and think like a professional.
The specialized knowledge and skills you gain through the program will prepare you for a successful career at Openmesh.
Why Join Us
Lead a revolutionary product that is reshaping the landscape of data management and accessibility.
Collaborate with a global community of innovators and thought leaders in the decentralized space.
Make a significant impact on how data is accessed and utilized worldwide, promoting transparency, efficiency, and democratization.
Enjoy a dynamic, challenging, and rewarding work environment, along with competitive compensation and benefits.
Beyond academic skills, we are most interested in what makes you unique: the personal qualities, outside interests and achievements beyond university that demonstrate the kind of person you are and the difference you will bring to the team.

Job Description
Join the team redefining how the world experiences design.
Hey, g'day, mabuhay, kia ora, 你好, hallo, vítejte!
Thanks for stopping by. We know job hunting can be a little time-consuming, and you're probably keen to find out what's on offer, so we'll get straight to the point.
Where and how you can work
Our flagship campus is in Sydney. We also have a campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth and Adelaide. But you have a choice in where and how you work, we trust our Canvanauts to choose the balance that empowers them and their team to achieve their goals.
What you'd be doing in this role
As a Staff Data Scientist in the Growth Supergroup, you’ll play a key role in shaping how Canva measures, optimises, and accelerates progress toward our foundational goals. You’ll partner closely with cross-functional teams to unlock insights, drive experimentation, and influence strategic decisions at scale.
Canva seeks to enhance its understanding of commercial metrics by designing causal models that link input metrics- like feature exposure and engagement - to revenue and Monthly Active Users (MAU). This role will validate relationships within Canva's Metrics Tree, quantifying their impact and influencing success definitions. As a key analytical resource for Monthly Business Reviews and a partner to leadership, your insights will directly shape company strategy and growth actions.
At the moment, this role is focused on:
Design and build causal models that quantify the relationships between input metrics (feature exposure, adoption, engagement, etc.) and component metrics to Canva's foundational goals (paid upgrades, user retention, user acquisition, etc.) — establishing which hypothesised links hold up and how strong they are.
Partner with embedded data science and analytics teams to design experiments and/or analytical approaches that test causal hypotheses, adapting methodology to the wide variety of contexts across Canva (short-run A/B tests, long-term holdouts, quasi-experimental methods where randomisation isn't feasible).
Own the causal layer of Canva's Metrics Tree — validating and quantifying the links between team-level input metrics and company-level outcomes, and feeding findings back into how teams set targets and define success. Over time, extend this framework to cover the UCM funnel as it matures.
Act as the analytical lead for Monthly Business Reviews in partnership with FGP Ops — onboarding team metrics, sense-checking what's being tracked, owning the MBR frontend in Airtable, and ensuring the MBR surfaces the right signals to leadership.
Partner with Analytics Engineering to embed validated metrics and causal findings into the Semantic Layer — enabling dimensional cuts, and the tooling teams need to track and investigate key metrics.
Drive a minimum standard of accountability and ownership on key output metrics across the organisation — partnering with teams in a consultative capacity to define data artefacts, SLAs, and alerting frameworks that ensure metrics are actively monitored and owned, without taking direct ownership of the metrics themselves.
Serve as a key analytical partner to leadership — stress-testing strategic assumptions, supporting pricing and commercial modelling, and providing analytical firepower on high-stakes decisions.
Develop and communicate clear, defensible points of view on what drives user value at Canva — both free and paid — and translate those into actionable recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Develop AI-powered tools and agents that amplify your analytical reach — enabling embedded teams to independently replicate and extend causal analysis, metric validation, and commercial modelling approaches without requiring direct involvement on every question.
You're probably a match if
You have deep expertise in causal inference and econometric methods, having worked with approaches like instrumental variables, difference-in-differences, synthetic control, or structural causal models in applied settings, not just academic ones.
You possess strong experimental design skills, with the judgment to recognise when a clean A/B test isn't feasible and the creativity to design credible alternatives.
You are fluent in SQL and Python as daily working tools, not just as skills listed on a CV, and you can build production-quality analytical code, not just notebooks.
You have the ability to transition between deep technical work and strategic communication — you can spend a week building a causal model and then distil it into a clear recommendation for a non-technical executive seamlessly.
You have experience partnering with cross-functional teams (product, growth, commercial) and translating their domain problems into well-defined analytical questions.
You possess a strong commercial instinct, naturally thinking about how analytical findings connect to revenue, pricing, and growth levers, not just statistical significance.
You are comfortable forming and defending a point of view. We don't need someone who presents options — we need someone who lands a recommendation and backs it with evidence.
You are curious about how AI and automation can extend analytical capability, excited about building tools that scale your impact beyond what you can personally touch.
About the team
The mission of the ‘Foundational Goals Performance’ team is to enhance overall commercial measurement results across Canva, ensuring a consistent path to achieving our growth targets. This challenge lies at the heart of Canva's identity, transforming our approach to product investments, fostering collaboration around growth, and equipping teams with the appropriate tools and metrics to facilitate these discussions. With this objective in mind, the team naturally collaborates across the entire organisation to drive Canva’s progress forward as a unified entity.

• Inclusive parental leave policy that supports all parents & carers
• An annual Vibe & Thrive allowance to support your wellbeing, social connection, office setup & more

We celebrate all types of skills and backgrounds at Canva so even if you don’t feel like your skills quite match what’s listed above - we still want to hear from you!
Please note that interviews are conducted virtually.
Before we jump into the responsibilities of the role. No matter what you come in knowing, you’ll be learning new things all the time and the Canva team will be there to support your growth.

Role Title: Senior Data Scientist in SPAI (2x positions available)
Join our Strategic Planning, Economics and Experience Branch at Ministry of Health for an exciting ongoing employment opportunity and be part of the team enriching health in millions of ways every day.
About us
We offer robust development and growth support to all our employees, ensuring you have the resources and opportunities to thrive in your career.
Our core values of collaboration, openness, respect, and empowerment are more than just words – they're the guiding principles that shape every aspect of our work.
Embrace a healthy work-life balance with our flexible/hybrid working hours.
To learn more about the Ministry and what benefits we offer, access our Employee Benefits Handbook.
About this role
With your skills and experience, you can contribute to the millions of ways we’re enhancing health and wellness while developing your career as part of the largest health organisation in Australia.
This role will provide you with an exciting opportunity to join the Service Planning Analytics and Insights team where you can influence key areas of planning for the NSW Health system.
We are seeking two high-performing individuals to join the Service Planning Analytics and Insights unit.  We are a team who collaborate with Local Health Districts, Specialty Health Networks, other Ministry of Health teams and NSW Health entities in relation to statewide service planning, to support the achievement of NSW Health’s service planning and reform objectives. As a Senior Data Scientist, you will be able to enhance your skills in data science through using a range of statistical analysis methods, tools and techniques to understand and simulate patterns of health care utilisation and project future health service needs.

Qualifications in Data Science/Data Analytics, Actuarial Mathematics and Statistics along with previous experience in health data, linked data sets and population health data and analysis would be considered advantageous for this role.

Crown Clerk 9/10, starting salary from $129,464 - $142,665 plus Super and annual leave loading, with a 35-hour work week, work location- 1 Reserve Road, St Leonards
For more information, please read the full role description.
What you'll be doing
Responsible for autonomously completing advanced data analysis to support systemwide planning initiatives and projection patterns of healthcare utilisation.
Responsible for evaluating and selecting appropriate modelling techniques (e.g. for emerging DSM requirements), fitting parameters and reviewing output autonomously, communicating findings effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
Demonstrate an ability to promote and trial new methods within the DSM and other modelling and analytics, and identify project opportunities related to process improvement, using new and emerging data science and data engineering techniques.
Demonstrate a flexible response to requests for data and information, often at short notice, against a background of high work volumes and demands for accurate, expert responses to complex issues, requiring the integration of diverse sources of information and strong written, verbal communication, interpersonal and consultation skills.
Develop and maintain collaborative relationships with managers in other areas of the Ministry as well as data scientists, data analysts, health planners and health researchers in Local Health Districts involved in planning, monitoring and evaluating health services and health system innovation.
About you
We are seeking motivated and committed individuals who can support the work of NSW Health with:
Relevant tertiary qualifications and / or relevant experience in Data Science, Data Analytics, Actuarial, Mathematics, and Statistics. Demonstrated intellectual curiosity and openness to explore new analytics techniques and data engineering principles and tools is essential.
Demonstrated experience with a range of analytics methodologies including predictive modelling, ideally with Generalised Linear Models (GLMs), discriminant analysis, time-series forecasting or other relevant statistical or computational methods, demonstrating proficiency in R and other relevant programming applications.
Extensive experience conducting and interpreting statistical analyses of population-based health administrative or other health related data, including linked datasets, using a range of analytic tools and methodologies, including temporal and sub-group adjusted and/or linked data analyses, to understand and simulate patterns of healthcare utilisation.
Strong collaborative and relationship-building skills, effectively working in dynamic, multidisciplinary environments with clinicians, managers, staff, and external stakeholders.
Consistently demonstrates behaviours that reinforce the CORE Values of our organisation; Collaboration, Openness, Respect and Empowerment.

title: Data Scientist
description:
Your opportunity
Join our Data & Insights team where curiosity meets impact. As a Data Scientist, you'll help translate big questions into actionable insights, turning complex data into models and stories that guide smarter decisions across the business. Whether it’s forecasting customer behaviour, uncovering growth opportunities or driving operational improvements, your work will directly contribute to shaping better outcomes for our customers and community. If you're passionate about data and want to see the real-world effect of your models, this is your opportunity.

Exploring large, curated datasets to uncover trends, patterns, and anomalies.
Designing and building models using statistical and machine learning techniques.
Hypo-thesis, optimisations and deep dives to support decision-making across teams.
Collaborating with cross-functional teams including Product, Marketing, and Operations.
Communicating insights clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders.
Working within cloud environments (e.g. AWS or GCP) using Python and/or R, SQL, and industry-standard libraries and visualisation tools (e.g tableau, powerbi etc).

We are seeking a curious, hands-on Data Scientist who enjoys solving complex problems and working closely with diverse teams. Strategic: Able to translate business problems into analytical frameworks with measurable outcomes.
Commercial: Understand the value of data in driving business performance and customer outcomes.
Collaborative: Work effectively across disciplines, aligning data solutions with broader team goals.
Innovative: Comfortable experimenting with new tools, methods, and ways of thinking to solve problems.

Scentre Group owns 42 Westfield destinations across Australia and New Zealand. We create extraordinary places and experiences that connect and enrich communities.
We are focused on our customers and creating more reasons for more people to visit our Westfield destinations more often and for longer.
With approximately 75 professions within our business, our team has the expertise to design, construct, operate, manage and market our Westfield destinations and platforms.

Diversity, equity and inclusion underpins our culture, and our vision is that ‘Everyone Belongs’. We foster a workplace experience where everyone feels valued, supported and motivated to realise their full potential.
We aspire to create a workforce reflective of the communities in which we operate and encourage applications from everyone regardless of age, gender, ethnicity, cultural background, faith, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or life stage.
We offer a range of unique benefits designed to support your wellbeing, career development and lifestyle, including five days paid Life Leave on top of your four weeks annual leave (pro-rated for part-time), 18 weeks gender neutral paid parental leave for primary carers, with no qualifying period and super paid for the duration of the leave period and free parking at your local Westfield destination.

title: Lead Machine Learning Engineer

DingGo is on a mission to modernise how Australia’s automotive ecosystem handles vehicle damage and repair — from first notice of loss through to repair completion. Our market leading data-driven platform serves panelbeaters, fleet operators, and insurers with tools that streamline the end-to-end crash management process through workflow automation and crash intelligence that helps fleets, insurers, and repairers make smarter, faster decisions.
We’re a fast-growing, product-led company with deep domain expertise and ambitious plans for AU/NZ and beyond.
We’re looking for a hands-on Lead ML Engineer to join our growing team. This is a pivotal, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of AI and Product — you’ll be responsible for the full lifecycle of our AI/ML capabilities, from architecture and experimentation through to production deployment and ongoing monitoring.
Your work will directly power DingGo’s suite of AI products: damage detection, repair cost estimation, document intelligence, and more. You’ll work closely with our Head of Data, AI & New Products , data scientists, and product squads to ship real AI features into the hands of real customers.
We value curiosity, rigour, and a bias for impact. If you want to build AI that actually matters— that gets used by real businesses every day — this is the role for you.
Relevant Skills & Technologies
AI/ML Engineering
Computer Vision
Document AI (DocAI)
Large Language Models (LLMs)
MLOps
Data Science
Python
AWS (Lambda, S3, ECS, CloudWatch, Fargate)
Snowflake
Docker
MLflow
BitBucket / Git
FastAPI / REST APIs
SQL

Required Qualification and Experience
• A Bachelor’s degree or higher qualification required
• Minimum two years of hands-on ML/AI engineering experience, including production deployments
• Strong Python engineering skills: clean, testable, maintainable code
• Proven computer vision experience — image classification, object detection, damage assessment, or similar
• Experience working with LLMs in production: prompt engineering, evaluation frameworks, guardrails, and cost management
• Document AI / unstructured data processing experience (PDFs, forms, images of documents)
• Practical MLOps experience: model versioning, inference pipelines, orchestration, and monitoring (MLflow or equivalent)
• Strong AWS experience: Lambda, ECS, S3, CloudWatch; familiarity with serverless and containerised deployments
• Solid SQL and data skills; experience with Snowflake or a comparable cloud data warehouse
• Experience designing and building REST APIs and backend services in Python (e.g. FastAPI)
• Ability to define and own AI solution architecture, not just implement tasks
• Comfortable working in an early-stage, fast-moving product environment with shifting priorities
Key Responsibilities
AI/ML Model Development & Evaluation
• Design, develop, train, and fine-tune computer vision and multimodal ML models
• Build and maintain LLM-powered pipelines for document intelligence, repair estimation, and structured data extraction
• Develop rigorous evaluation frameworks for model quality, regression testing, and performance benchmarking
• Implement model observability and drift monitoring to maintain quality in production
• Conduct AI R&D: experiment with new architectures, techniques, and open-source models to advance DingGo’s capabilities
LLM Engineering
• Define the target prompt architecture for LLM-powered features
• Build and maintain guardrails, safety layers, and output validation for LLM features in customer-facing products
• Evaluate and benchmark LLM providers (OpenAI, Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, open- source) to optimise quality and cost
• Manage LLM usage costs and ensure efficient, responsible use of inference compute AI Solution Architecture
• Define and own DingGo’s target-state AI/ML stack, selecting tools, frameworks, and infrastructure components that balance capability, cost, and operational complexity
• Design the optimal architecture for each AI feature: real-time vs. batch, synchronous vs. async, cloud-managed vs. self-hosted
• Evaluate open-source tools (Hugging Face, LangChain, LlamaIndex, MLflow, Ray, etc.) and AWS-native services to build a pragmatic, scalable stack
AI Product Development
• Collaborate closely with Product and Data teams to translate product requirements into AI/ML feature designs
• Embed AI capabilities within DingGo’s SaaS platform, including new standalone AI products for fleets, insurers, and repairers
• Contribute to sprint planning, technical scoping, and delivery estimates for AI features
• Ensure AI features are explainable, auditable, and meet the expectations of enterprise and insurance clients
MLOps & Production Deployment
• Build and maintain CI/CD pipelines for ML models using BitBucket Pipelines, Docker, and AWS (ECS, Lambda)
• Work with DevOps to deploy and scale AI services in production, with clear runbooks and rollback procedures
• Maintain MLflow (or equivalent) for experiment tracking, model registry, and deployment artefacts
• Manage containerised model serving and inference endpoints optimised for latency and throughput
Monitoring, Security & Cost Management
• Implement production monitoring for model performance, data quality, and system health using AWS CloudWatch and custom dashboards
• Ensure AI systems meet DingGo’s ISO 27001 compliance requirements, including data handling, access controls, and audit logging
• Proactively manage total cost of ownership (TCO) for AI/ML infrastructure, identifying and acting on cost optimisation opportunities
• Maintain high availability SLAs for customer-facing AI features
What Success Looks Like at 12 Months
• Multiple new AI products shipped and live with paying clients across fleet, insurance, and repairer segments
• DingGo’s target-state AI/ML stack is defined, documented, and stood up — providing a clear foundation for the next 2–3 years of product growth
• Model quality metrics (accuracy, precision, recall, latency) are tracked, visible, and consistently improving across core computer vision and LLM features
• A robust MLOps practice in place: repeatable deployment pipelines, model versioning, automated evals, and monitoring from day one
• ISO 27001 compliance maintained across all AI systems, with clear data handling policies and audit trails
• AI infrastructure costs are tracked and optimised, with a clear view of per-product and per-client unit economics
• You’re a trusted technical voice within the business — influencing product direction, architectural decisions, and the team’s engineering culture

Our flagship campus is in Sydney, with a second campus in Melbourne and co-working spaces in Brisbane, Perth, Adelaide, and Auckland, NZ. You have flexibility in how and where you work — whether that's from one of our spaces, from home, or a mix of both. This role is remote-friendly within Australia, so you can choose the setup that empowers you and your team to do your best work.
Job Description
About the team
We aim to build the world’s richest Ecosystem of apps for visual design and communications that supercharge Canva’s ability to meet the diverse needs of a billion users and drive Canva’s MAU growth.
With the proliferation of innovations in generative AI and as large organizations have increasingly complex workflows to manage their designs, Canva is well poised to become the platform that simplifies access and discovery of services related to visual design. We are already working with hundreds of developers to enable access to these exciting products with our Apps SDK and Canva public REST API!
As one of the groups in Ecosystem, the Integrations and Solutions Group builds Canva's AI integration layer — the infrastructure that connects Canva's design capabilities to the world's leading AI assistants. Our teams own the MCP platform, AI-optimised tools and APIs, evaluation frameworks, and the agent architecture that powers millions of AI-driven design interactions. We work directly with partners like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and we're in the middle of a strategic shift from protocol-first integrations toward intelligent, Canva-hosted design agents.
As a Staff Machine Learning Engineer, you'll play a critical role in defining how AI platforms experience Canva — driving the technical standards, evaluation frameworks, and architectural decisions that ensure our integrations are reliable, measurable, and evolving with a rapidly changing ecosystem.
What you’d be doing in this role
As Canva scales change continues to be part of our DNA. But we like to think that's all part of the fun. So this will give you the flavour of the type of things you'll be working on when you start, but this will likely evolve.

Drive the design and evolution of AI-ready tools and APIs that enable LLM platforms (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and others) to reliably interact with Canva's design capabilities — defining the patterns and standards that other teams adopt for tool descriptions, payload structures, and intent-based interfaces. Pioneer agent-to-agent communication approaches.
Own and evolve evaluation frameworks that systematically measure tool-use accuracy across platforms — defining what "good" looks like for proxy-based fast evals and real-client production evals, and ensuring these frameworks scale as we add platforms and capabilities.
Shape Canva's agent architecture — making strategic technical decisions about where intelligence should live (in external LLMs vs Canva-hosted agents), building the orchestration layers that allow third-party providers to invoke Canva's design tools at scale, and driving automation of complex workflows like marketing campaigns.
Define and build observability systems that give multiple teams visibility into how AI assistants consume Canva's tools in production — identifying failure patterns, setting quality benchmarks, and closing the loop between production data and continuous improvement.
Work across team and platform boundaries — proactively identifying problems not yet defined, understanding behavioural quirks across LLM platforms, and driving solutions that span the AI Integrations, API Capabilities, and Workflow Integrations teams.
Influence integration strategy with AI partners and internal teams — contributing to technical direction with OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google, and shaping how Canva's broader engineering organisation builds for AI consumption.

You've shipped LLM-powered systems into production and can quantify your impact — things like improving tool-call accuracy from X% to Y%, reducing agent error rates, cutting latency by Z%, or measurably improving user outcomes through better AI integration. We care about results, not just launches.
You proactively find and solve problems others haven't defined yet — you've identified gaps in how LLMs consume tools or APIs, scoped the problem across teams, and driven the fix without waiting for someone to hand you a brief.
You've built or owned evaluation pipelines end-to-end — designing metrics, building benchmarking infrastructure, and using data to make architectural decisions about AI integrations at scale.
You set technical standards that others follow — whether that's tool design patterns, API contracts for AI agents, documentation quality, or observability practices. Your work becomes the reference point.
You can connect external ecosystem changes to internal strategy — when a new LLM capability drops or a partner shifts their architecture, you can quickly assess the implications for Canva and re-prioritise accordingly.
You're proficient in Python and familiar with ML frameworks, and equally comfortable working with TypeScript/Node.js and cloud infrastructure (Cloudflare Workers, AWS, or similar).
You thrive in cross-team, partner-facing work — influencing engineering, product, and external AI platform teams to shape integration strategy. You're comfortable operating across team boundaries without formal authority.
You're energised by ambiguity and pace — the AI ecosystem is evolving rapidly, and you bring clarity and momentum rather than waiting for direction.

The primary aim of this event is to raise awareness about the importance and urgency of solving the problem of concentrated power over our data and information technology (IT) technologies.

We want to put a halt to trusting centralized systems and handing over our future to them. description:
We’re not looking for someone who builds from scratch on a clean system with unlimited time and budget.
Snowflake Data Architect needed
We’re looking for someone who has inherited a broken, multi-source financial data environment and rebuilt it into something the business actually trusts. Then wired it up for AI. 🚀
“That’s not a moon. That’s a data platform with no governance, no reconciliation, and six different definitions of revenue.”
The Role
You will own the architecture, build, and ongoing integrity of our data and AI platform. This means designing for financial accuracy today and AI-readiness tomorrow. You are hands-on. You write the models, own the pipelines, and sit in the room when the CFO asks why the numbers don’t match.
This is not a strategy role. This is not a documentation role. You build, you own, you deliver.
The business is at an inflection point. We have real transaction volume, real compliance obligations, and real ambitions to embed AI into how we make decisions. What we need now is someone who can make the data underneath all of that bulletproof, and then build the infrastructure that lets AI actually do something useful with it. 🤖
Financial Data Integrity 🔒
You will design and maintain a single source of truth in Snowflake. You will build and manage CDC pipelines that handle high transaction volumes cleanly and without data loss. You will implement snapshot and locking frameworks so month-end numbers stop shifting after financial close. You will solve identity resolution across multiple CRMs, payment systems, and trading platforms, building deterministic mapping logic that the business can rely on across jurisdictions.
You will build reconciliation frameworks that give the business genuine confidence in its numbers, closing the gap between what the source systems say and what the warehouse reports. Trust comes from reconciliation, not from dashboards that look nice.
AI and Machine Learning Infrastructure 🧠
On the AI side, you will architect the data foundations that make AI actually work. This means designing AI-ready data models from the ground up, building and maintaining feature stores for real-time ML consumption, and integrating LLM pipelines and RAG architectures into the platform in a way that is auditable and production-grade.
You will work closely with data scientists and product teams to ensure the data feeding into models is clean, consistent, and governed. You understand that a model is only as trustworthy as the data it was trained on, and that financial AI without data integrity is a liability, not an asset.
You will also help define how AI outputs are monitored, logged, and reconciled back to source data so the business can explain and defend what its models are doing. In a regulated environment, that matters enormously.
Platform Ownership 🛠️
Beyond building, you will own. That means quarterly data reviews with business stakeholders, ongoing data quality monitoring and alerting, schema evolution that doesn’t break downstream consumers, and a clear architectural roadmap that the business can invest behind with confidence.
What You’ve Done Before
You have rebuilt a messy financial data environment inside a fintech, payments company, neo-bank, prop trading firm, or similarly high-transaction business. You didn’t just design it on a whiteboard. You got your hands dirty, fixed the pipelines, wrote the dbt models, backfilled the history without corrupting the reporting, and got the CFO to trust the numbers again.
You have hands-on depth across Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, and CDC pipelines. You understand idempotent transformations, late-arriving data, and replay logic. You have implemented Type 2 slowly changing dimensions, point-in-time reconstruction, and immutable reporting tables. You know what month-end locking actually means in practice and you have built systems that enforce it.
On the AI side, you have worked with data scientists closely enough to understand what they actually need from the data platform. You have thought seriously about feature engineering, model serving infrastructure, and what it takes to make LLM outputs trustworthy in a production financial environment.
“Never tell me the odds” is not an engineering principle. You know your numbers, your pipelines, and exactly where the risk is. ⚡
You have worked in environments where data errors cost real money, triggered compliance incidents, or caused reporting restatements. You take data quality personally, because you have seen what happens when it fails.
The AI Piece 🤖
This is not an afterthought and it is not a future roadmap item. We are actively building a platform that will underpin AI-driven decision making across the business and we need someone who understands both sides of that equation.
You will shape how we approach LLM integration, how we build and serve features for ML models, and how we ensure AI outputs can be trusted, audited, and explained to a regulator if necessary.
You will have strong opinions about what makes a feature store actually useful versus theoretically interesting, and you will have the scars to back those opinions up.
If you have designed data platforms with downstream AI and ML consumption baked into the architecture from day one, you will be at home here. If you have only bolted AI onto an existing platform as an afterthought, we will know.
Must Haves ✅
Snowflake, dbt, Airflow, CDC pipelines, and PowerBI. High-transaction financial environment experience. Strong understanding of AI and ML data requirements including feature engineering, model serving infrastructure, and LLM-ready pipeline design. A track record of delivering reconciled, auditable, trustworthy financial data. Someone who builds and owns, not just advises and moves on.
Nice to Haves 👍
CFD trading, payments, or regulated environment exposure. Multi-currency and multi-entity data modelling. RAG pipeline design and LLM integration experience. Familiarity with ASIC, FCA, or MAS regulated environments. Experience designing data platforms that feed both operational AI and compliance reporting simultaneously.
What You Won’t Find Here 🚫
Someone who produces architectural documents but doesn’t write code. Someone who wants to start from zero with a greenfield build and a blank canvas. Someone who has only ever worked in SaaS marketing analytics and thinks that counts as financial data experience. A consultant who delivers and disappears.
If that’s you, this role is not for you. If it isn’t, keep reading.

Requirements
Job Title: Generative AI Engineer
Location: Sydney
Employment Type: Full-time / Contract
Start Date: Immediate
About the Role:
We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Generative AI Engineer to join our team and contribute to cutting-edge AI solutions. This role involves designing, developing, and deploying generative AI models and applications, with a strong focus on Large Language Models (LLMs), Python programming, and cloud-based infrastructure.
You will work closely with cross-functional teams to build intelligent systems that leverage generative AI capabilities for real-world applications.
Key Responsibilities:
Design, develop, and fine-tune Generative AI models using LLMs (e.g., GPT, LLaMA, Claude, Mistral).
Build scalable and efficient pipelines for training and deploying GenAI models.
Integrate GenAI capabilities into enterprise applications and services.
Collaborate with data scientists, ML engineers, and product teams to define use cases and deliver AI-powered solutions.
Optimize model performance and ensure responsible AI practices.
Maintain and improve existing GenAI systems and tools.
Document processes, model architectures, and deployment strategies.
Required Skills & Experience:
Strong expertise in Python for AI/ML development, including libraries such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face Transformers, LangChain, etc.
Hands-on experience with Large Language Models (LLMs) and Generative AI frameworks.
Experience in building and deploying AI models in production environments.
Familiarity with prompt engineering, fine-tuning, and model evaluation techniques.
Understanding of NLP, deep learning, and transformer architectures.
Experience with REST APIs and integrating AI models into applications.
Preferred / Added Advantage:
Exposure to Cloud Engineering and deployment on platforms like Azure and AWS.
Experience with containerization (Docker), orchestration (Kubernetes), and CI/CD pipelines.
Knowledge of data privacy, security, and ethical AI considerations.
Experience with vector databases (e.g., FAISS, Pinecone) and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG).
What We Offer:
Opportunity to work on cutting-edge GenAI projects.
Collaborative and innovative work environment.
Flexible work arrangements.
Competitive compensation aligned with market standards.
Benefits
We welcome applications from all members of society irrespective of age, sex, disability, sexual orientation, race, religion, or belief. We offer you great opportunities within a dynamically growing consultancy.
